manualTestCases.description: Verify that Playwright framework successfully connects to BigQuery database using service account credentials.
manualTestCases.title: Validate BigQuery Database Connection
manualTestCases.expectedResult: Playwright should establish a successful connection with BigQuery without any authentication or permission errors.
steps: 1. Configure BigQuery credentials in .env file.
2. Run Playwright test execution.
3. Trigger database connection method.
4. Check console logs for successful connection.
1. Launch application using Playwright.
2. Navigate to Employee page.
3. Capture total records count from UI.
4. Execute COUNT query in BigQuery.
5. Compare UI count with DB count.
manualTestCases.description: Verify that the total employee count displayed in UI matches the BigQuery database count.
manualTestCases.expectedResult: Employee count displayed in UI should exactly match the count returned from BigQuery database.
manualTestCases.title: Validate Employee Table Data Count

steps: 1. Open Employee listing page.
2. Capture employee names from UI table.
3. Execute SELECT query in BigQuery.
4. Fetch employee_name column data.
5. Compare UI data with DB data.
manualTestCases.expectedResult: All employee names displayed in UI should match the employee_name values fetched from BigQuery.
manualTestCases.title: Validate Employee Name Data Between UI and BigQuery
manualTestCases.description: Verify that employee names displayed in UI match the values stored in BigQuery table.

manualTestCases.expectedResult: API response data should match the records returned from BigQuery database.

manualTestCases.description: Verify that API response data matches records stored in BigQuery database.
steps: 1. Trigger API request using Playwright.
2. Capture API response data.
3. Execute corresponding SELECT query in BigQuery.
4. Fetch database records.
5. Compare API response with DB data.

manualTestCases.title: Validate Sorting Functionality with BigQuery
manualTestCases.expectedResult: UI sorting order should match the sorted order returned from BigQuery.

BUSINESS REQUIREMENTS DOCUMENT (BRD)

E-Commerce Application – Flipkart-like Platform

Document Version

1.0

Date

11-Sep-2026

Document Status

Draft

Prepared By

QA / Business Analysis Team

1. Introduction

1.1 Purpose

The purpose of this document is to define the business requirements for an e-commerce platform similar to Flipkart. This document is a sample/fictional BRD created for learning, Business Analysis, and QA/testing practice.

1.2 Business Objective

Increase online product sales.

Provide a simple and user-friendly shopping experience.

Support multiple payment methods.

Provide order tracking and delivery visibility.

Improve customer engagement through ratings and reviews.

Provide administrators with effective product and order management.

Reduce manual order-processing activities.

2. Scope

2.1 In Scope

User registration and login

Product categories, search, filtering and sorting

Product details

Wishlist and shopping cart

Address management

Checkout and online payment

Order placement and tracking

Order cancellation and product returns

Refund processing

Ratings and reviews

Customer notifications

Admin product, user, order and report management

2.2 Out of Scope

International shipping

Cryptocurrency payments

Physical-store management

Seller warehouse management

AI-based shopping assistant

3. Stakeholders

Stakeholder

Responsibility

Customer

Browse and purchase products

Admin

Manage application and users

Seller

Manage products and inventory

Delivery Partner

Deliver customer orders

Payment Gateway

Process online payments

Business Team

Define business requirements

Development Team

Develop application

QA Team

Test application

Support Team

Handle customer issues

4. User Roles

4.1 Customer

Create an account and log in.

Search and browse products.

Add products to wishlist/cart.

Purchase products and make payments.

Track, cancel, or return eligible orders.

Submit ratings and reviews.

4.2 Seller

Add and update products.

Manage inventory.

View orders and update order status.

View sales information.

4.3 Administrator

Manage users and sellers.

Manage products and categories.

Manage orders and payments.

Generate business reports.

5. Functional Requirements

ID

Requirement

Business Requirement

FR-01

User Registration

Users shall be able to register using name, mobile number/email, password and confirmation password. Email/mobile must be unique and verification may be required.

FR-02

User Login

Registered users shall be able to log in using valid email/mobile and password. Invalid credentials must show an appropriate error message. Forgot-password functionality shall be supported.

FR-03

Product Search

Users shall be able to search products using product name, brand, category and keywords.

FR-04

Product Categories

Products shall be organized into categories such as Electronics, Mobiles, Fashion, Home & Furniture, Grocery, Appliances, Books, Beauty and Sports.

FR-05

Product Filtering

Users shall be able to filter products by price, brand, rating, availability, discount, category and features.

FR-06

Product Sorting

Users shall be able to sort by price low-to-high, price high-to-low, rating, popularity, newest arrivals and discounts.

FR-07

Product Details

The product page shall display product name, images, price, discount, description, specifications, ratings, reviews, availability, delivery information and seller information.

FR-08

Add to Cart

Users shall be able to add available products to the cart. Cart shall show quantity, price, discount, delivery charges and final amount.

FR-09

Update Cart

Users shall be able to increase/decrease quantity and remove products. Totals shall update accordingly.

FR-10

Wishlist

Users shall be able to save products to a wishlist, remove them, or move them to the cart.

FR-11

Address Management

Users shall be able to add, edit, delete and set a default delivery address.

FR-12

Checkout

Users shall select an address, review products, apply coupons, select payment method, review order summary and place the order.

FR-13

Payment

The system shall support UPI, cards, net banking, wallets and Cash on Delivery. Payment status and transaction details shall be captured securely.

FR-14

Order Management

After successful order placement, the customer shall receive an order confirmation containing Order ID, products, quantity, price, address, payment method, date and expected delivery.

FR-15

Order Tracking

Customers shall be able to view the current status and tracking information for their orders.

FR-16

Order Cancellation

Customers shall be able to cancel eligible orders. Cancellation reason shall be captured and applicable refunds initiated.

FR-17

Product Return

Customers shall be able to request returns for eligible products with a selected return reason.

FR-18

Refund

For eligible cancelled/returned orders, the system shall initiate and track refunds through Initiated, Processing and Completed states.

FR-19

Ratings & Reviews

Eligible customers shall be able to submit 1–5 star ratings and written reviews for purchased products.

FR-20

Notifications

The system shall send relevant email, SMS or push notifications for registration, order, payment, shipping, delivery, cancellation, return and refund events.

6. Order Lifecycle

Order Placed → Confirmed → Packed → Shipped → Out for Delivery → Delivered

7. Admin Requirements

7.1 Product Management

Add products

Edit products

Delete/deactivate products

Update prices

Manage inventory

7.2 User Management

View users

Activate/deactivate users

View user details

7.3 Order Management

View orders

Update order status

View cancelled orders

View returned orders

View refund status

7.4 Reports

Sales report

Product report

Customer report

Order report

Revenue report

Return/refund report

8. Non-Functional Requirements

Area

Requirement

Performance

Pages and search results should respond within acceptable limits under normal load.

Security

Use secure password storage, role-based access control, protected APIs and secure handling of sensitive data.

Availability

Application should provide high availability and minimize downtime.

Scalability

System should support growth in users, products, orders and transactions.

Usability

Application should provide simple navigation, responsive UI, clear errors and consistent design.

9. Assumptions

Users have internet connectivity.

Payment gateway services are available.

Delivery partners are integrated with the system.

Sellers provide accurate product information.

Users provide valid delivery details.

Product inventory is updated regularly.

10. Dependencies

Payment Gateway

SMS Gateway

Email Service

Maps/Location Service

Delivery/Logistics Service

Database

Authentication Service

11. Risks and Mitigation

Risk

Impact

Mitigation

Payment failure

High

Retry and payment-status handling

Server downtime

High

High-availability infrastructure

Incorrect inventory

High

Real-time inventory updates

Security breach

Critical

Security controls, access control and monitoring

Delivery delay

Medium

Logistics tracking and status visibility

High traffic

High

Scalable infrastructure and performance testing

12. Acceptance Criteria

Users can successfully register and log in.

Users can search, filter and sort products.

Users can add, update and remove products from the cart.

Users can successfully place orders.

Payment status is correctly captured.

Orders can be tracked.

Eligible orders can be cancelled or returned.

Refund status is correctly updated.

Admin can manage products and orders.

Critical and high-severity defects are resolved before release.

Security and performance requirements are satisfied.

13. Sample End-to-End Business Flow

User Registration → User Login → Browse / Search Product → View Product Details → Add to Cart → Select Address → Apply Coupon → Select Payment Method → Make Payment → Order Confirmation → Order Processing → Order Shipped → Out for Delivery → Order Delivered → Rating & Review

14. QA Traceability Example

BRD Requirement

Sample Test Scenario

FR-02 – User Login

Login with valid credentials

FR-02 – User Login

Login with invalid password

FR-03 – Product Search

Search using valid product keyword

FR-05 – Product Filtering

Filter products by price range

FR-08 – Add to Cart

Add an available product to cart

FR-12 – Checkout

Complete checkout with valid address

FR-13 – Payment

Complete payment using UPI

FR-15 – Order Tracking

Verify order status after shipment

FR-16 – Cancellation

Cancel an eligible order

FR-19 – Ratings

Submit rating after successful delivery

15. QA Process Mapping

BRD → Requirements → Test Scenarios → Test Cases → Automation → Test Execution → Defect Reporting → Retesting/Regression → RTM → Test Closure

16. Approval

Role

Name

Signature

Date

Business Owner







Project Manager







Business Analyst







QA Lead

BUSINESS REQUIREMENTS DOCUMENT (BRD)

E-Commerce Application – Flipkart-like Platform

Document Version

1.0

Date

11-Sep-2026

Document Status

Draft

Prepared By

QA / Business Analysis Team

1. Introduction

1.1 Purpose

The purpose of this document is to define the business requirements for an e-commerce platform similar to Flipkart. This document is a sample/fictional BRD created for learning, Business Analysis, and QA/testing practice.

1.2 Business Objective

Increase online product sales.

Provide a simple and user-friendly shopping experience.

Support multiple payment methods.

Provide order tracking and delivery visibility.

Improve customer engagement through ratings and reviews.

Provide administrators with effective product and order management.

Reduce manual order-processing activities.

2. Scope

2.1 In Scope

User registration and login

Product categories, search, filtering and sorting

Product details

Wishlist and shopping cart

Address management

Checkout and online payment

Order placement and tracking

Order cancellation and product returns

Refund processing

Ratings and reviews

Customer notifications

Admin product, user, order and report management

2.2 Out of Scope

International shipping

Cryptocurrency payments

Physical-store management

Seller warehouse management

AI-based shopping assistant

3. Stakeholders

Stakeholder

Responsibility

Customer

Browse and purchase products

Admin

Manage application and users

Seller

Manage products and inventory

Delivery Partner

Deliver customer orders

Payment Gateway

Process online payments

Business Team

Define business requirements

Development Team

Develop application

QA Team

Test application

Support Team

userStories.fileTextContent:
BUSINESS REQUIREMENTS DOCUMENT (BRD)

E-Commerce Application – Flipkart-like Platform

Document Version

1.0

Date

11-Sep-2026

Document Status

Draft

Prepared By

QA / Business Analysis Team

1. Introduction

1.1 Purpose

The purpose of this document is to define the business requirements for an e-commerce platform similar to Flipkart. This document is a sample/fictional BRD created for learning, Business Analysis, and QA/testing practice.

1.2 Business Objective

Increase online product sales.

Provide a simple and user-friendly shopping experience.

Support multiple payment methods.

Provide order tracking and delivery visibility.

Improve customer engagement through ratings and reviews.

Provide administrators with effective product and order management.

Reduce manual order-processing activities.

2. Scope

2.1 In Scope

User registration and login

Product categories, search, filtering and sorting

Product details

Wishlist and shopping cart

Address management

Checkout and online payment

Order placement and tracking

Order cancellation and product returns

Refund processing

Ratings and reviews

Customer notifications

Admin product, user, order and report management

2.2 Out of Scope

International shipping

Cryptocurrency payments

Physical-store management

Seller warehouse management

AI-based shopping assistant

3. Stakeholders

Stakeholder

Responsibility

Customer

Browse and purchase products

Admin

Manage application and users

Seller

Manage products and inventory

Delivery Partner

Deliver customer orders

Payment Gateway

Process online payments

Business Team

Define business requirements

Development Team

Develop application

QA Team

Test application

Support Team

Handle customer issues

4. User Roles

4.1 Customer

Create an account and log in.

Search and browse products.

Add products to wishlist/cart.

Purchase products and make payments.

Track, cancel, or return eligible orders.

Submit ratings and reviews.

4.2 Seller

Add and update products.

Manage inventory.

View orders and update order status.

View sales information.

4.3 Administrator

Manage users and sellers.

Manage products and categories.

Manage orders and payments.

Generate business reports.

5. Functional Requirements

ID

Requirement

Business Requirement

FR-01

User Registration

Users shall be able to register using name, mobile number/email, password and confirmation password. Email/mobile must be unique and verification may be required.

FR-02

User Login

Registered users shall be able to log in using valid email/mobile and password. Invalid credentials must show an appropriate error message. Forgot-password functionality shall be supported.

FR-03

Product Search

Users shall be able to search products using product name, brand, category and keywords.

FR-04

Product Categories

Products shall be organized into categories such as Electronics, Mobiles, Fashion, Home & Furniture, Grocery, Appliances, Books, Beauty and Sports.

FR-05

Product Filtering

Users shall be able to filter products by price, brand, rating, availability, discount, category and features.

FR-06

Product Sorting

Users shall be able to sort by price low-to-high, price high-to-low, rating, popularity, newest arrivals and discounts.

FR-07

Product Details

The product page shall display product name, images, price, discount, description, specifications, ratings, reviews, availability, delivery information and seller information.

FR-08

Add to Cart

Users shall be able to add available products to the cart. Cart shall show quantity, price, discount, delivery charges and final amount.

FR-09

Update Cart

Users shall be able to increase/decrease quantity and remove products. Totals shall update accordingly.

FR-10

Wishlist

Users shall be able to save products to a wishlist, remove them, or move them to the cart.

FR-11

Address Management

Users shall be able to add, edit, delete and set a default delivery address.

FR-12

Checkout

Users shall select an address, review products, apply coupons, select payment method, review order summary and place the order.

FR-13

Payment

The system shall support UPI, cards, net banking, wallets and Cash on Delivery. Payment status and transaction details shall be captured securely.

FR-14

Order Management

After successful order placement, the customer shall receive an order confirmation containing Order ID, products, quantity, price, address, payment method, date and expected delivery.

FR-15

Order Tracking

Customers shall be able to view the current status and tracking information for their orders.

FR-16

Order Cancellation

Customers shall be able to cancel eligible orders. Cancellation reason shall be captured and applicable refunds initiated.

FR-17

Product Return

Customers shall be able to request returns for eligible products with a selected return reason.

FR-18

Refund

For eligible cancelled/returned orders, the system shall initiate and track refunds through Initiated, Processing and Completed states.

FR-19

Ratings & Reviews

Eligible customers shall be able to submit 1–5 star ratings and written reviews for purchased products.

FR-20

Notifications

The system shall send relevant email, SMS or push notifications for registration, order, payment, shipping, delivery, cancellation, return and refund events.

6. Order Lifecycle

Order Placed → Confirmed → Packed → Shipped → Out for Delivery → Delivered

7. Admin Requirements

7.1 Product Management

Add products

Edit products

Delete/deactivate products

Update prices

Manage inventory

7.2 User Management

View users

Activate/deactivate users

View user details

7.3 Order Management

View orders

Update order status

View cancelled orders

View returned orders

View refund status

7.4 Reports

Sales report

Product report

Customer report

Order report

Revenue report

Return/refund report

8. Non-Functional Requirements

Area

Requirement

Performance

Pages and search results should respond within acceptable limits under normal load.

Security

Use secure password storage, role-based access control, protected APIs and secure handling of sensitive data.

Availability

Application should provide high availability and minimize downtime.

Scalability

System should support growth in users, products, orders and transactions.

Usability

Application should provide simple navigation, responsive UI, clear errors and consistent design.

9. Assumptions

Users have internet connectivity.

Payment gateway services are available.

Delivery partners are integrated with the system.

Sellers provide accurate product information.

Users provide valid delivery details.

Product inventory is updated regularly.

10. Dependencies

Payment Gateway

SMS Gateway

Email Service

Maps/Location Service

Delivery/Logistics Service

Database

Authentication Service

11. Risks and Mitigation

Risk

Impact

Mitigation

Payment failure

High

Retry and payment-status handling

Server downtime

High

High-availability infrastructure

Incorrect inventory

High

Real-time inventory updates

Security breach

Critical

Security controls, access control and monitoring

Delivery delay

Medium

Logistics tracking and status visibility

High traffic

High

Scalable infrastructure and performance testing

12. Acceptance Criteria

Users can successfully register and log in.

Users can search, filter and sort products.

Users can add, update and remove products from the cart.

Users can successfully place orders.

Payment status is correctly captured.

Orders can be tracked.

Eligible orders can be cancelled or returned.

Refund status is correctly updated.

Admin can manage products and orders.

Critical and high-severity defects are resolved before release.

Security and performance requirements are satisfied.

13. Sample End-to-End Business Flow

User Registration → User Login → Browse / Search Product → View Product Details → Add to Cart → Select Address → Apply Coupon → Select Payment Method → Make Payment → Order Confirmation → Order Processing → Order Shipped → Out for Delivery → Order Delivered → Rating & Review

14. QA Traceability Example

BRD Requirement

Sample Test Scenario

FR-02 – User Login

Login with valid credentials

FR-02 – User Login

Login with invalid password

FR-03 – Product Search

Search using valid product keyword

FR-05 – Product Filtering

Filter products by price range

FR-08 – Add to Cart

Add an available product to cart

FR-12 – Checkout

Complete checkout with valid address

FR-13 – Payment

Complete payment using UPI

FR-15 – Order Tracking

Verify order status after shipment

FR-16 – Cancellation

Cancel an eligible order

FR-19 – Ratings

Submit rating after successful delivery

15. QA Process Mapping

BRD → Requirements → Test Scenarios → Test Cases → Automation → Test Execution → Defect Reporting → Retesting/Regression → RTM → Test Closure

16. Approval

Signature

userStories.fileTextContent:
BUSINESS REQUIREMENTS DOCUMENT (BRD)

E-Commerce Application – Flipkart-like Platform

Document Version

1.0

Date

11-Sep-2026

Document Status

Draft

Prepared By

QA / Business Analysis Team

1. Introduction

1.1 Purpose

The purpose of this document is to define the business requirements for an e-commerce platform similar to Flipkart. This document is a sample/fictional BRD created for learning, Business Analysis, and QA/testing practice.

1.2 Business Objective

Increase online product sales.

Provide a simple and user-friendly shopping experience.

Support multiple payment methods.

Provide order tracking and delivery visibility.

Improve customer engagement through ratings and reviews.

Provide administrators with effective product and order management.

Reduce manual order-processing activities.

2. Scope

2.1 In Scope

User registration and login

Product categories, search, filtering and sorting

Product details

Wishlist and shopping cart

Address management

Checkout and online payment

Order placement and tracking

Order cancellation and product returns

Refund processing

Ratings and reviews

Customer notifications

Admin product, user, order and report management

2.2 Out of Scope

International shipping

Cryptocurrency payments

Physical-store management

Seller warehouse management

AI-based shopping assistant

3. Stakeholders

Stakeholder

Responsibility

Customer

Browse and purchase products

Admin

Manage application and users

Seller

Manage products and inventory

Delivery Partner

Deliver customer orders

Payment Gateway

Process online payments

Business Team

Define business requirements

Development Team

Develop application

QA Team

Test application

Support Team

Handle customer issues

4. User Roles

4.1 Customer

Create an account and log in.

Search and browse products.

Add products to wishlist/cart.

Purchase products and make payments.

Track, cancel, or return eligible orders.

Submit ratings and reviews.

4.2 Seller

Add and update products.

Manage inventory.

View orders and update order status.

View sales information.

4.3 Administrator

Manage users and sellers.

Manage products and categories.

Manage orders and payments.

Generate business reports.

5. Functional Requirements

ID

Requirement

Business Requirement

FR-01

User Registration

Users shall be able to register using name, mobile number/email, password and confirmation password. Email/mobile must be unique and verification may be required.

FR-02

User Login

Registered users shall be able to log in using valid email/mobile and password. Invalid credentials must show an appropriate error message. Forgot-password functionality shall be supported.

FR-03

Product Search

Users shall be able to search products using product name, brand, category and keywords.

FR-04

Product Categories

Products shall be organized into categories such as Electronics, Mobiles, Fashion, Home & Furniture, Grocery, Appliances, Books, Beauty and Sports.

FR-05

Product Filtering

Users shall be able to filter products by price, brand, rating, availability, discount, category and features.

FR-06

Product Sorting

Users shall be able to sort by price low-to-high, price high-to-low, rating, popularity, newest arrivals and discounts.

FR-07

Product Details

The product page shall display product name, images, price, discount, description, specifications, ratings, reviews, availability, delivery information and seller information.

FR-08

Add to Cart

Users shall be able to add available products to the cart. Cart shall show quantity, price, discount, delivery charges and final amount.

FR-09

Update Cart

Users shall be able to increase/decrease quantity and remove products. Totals shall update accordingly.

FR-10

Wishlist

Users shall be able to save products to a wishlist, remove them, or move them to the cart.

FR-11

Address Management

Users shall be able to add, edit, delete and set a default delivery address.

FR-12

Checkout

Users shall select an address, review products, apply coupons, select payment method, review order summary and place the order.

FR-13

Payment

The system shall support UPI, cards, net banking, wallets and Cash on Delivery. Payment status and transaction details shall be captured securely.

FR-14

Order Management

After successful order placement, the customer shall receive an order confirmation containing Order ID, products, quantity, price, address, payment method, date and expected delivery.

FR-15

Order Tracking

Customers shall be able to view the current status and tracking information for their orders.

FR-16

Order Cancellation

Customers shall be able to cancel eligible orders. Cancellation reason shall be captured and applicable refunds initiated.

FR-17

Product Return

Customers shall be able to request returns for eligible products with a selected return reason.

FR-18

Refund

For eligible cancelled/returned orders, the system shall initiate and track refunds through Initiated, Processing and Completed states.

FR-19

Ratings & Reviews

Eligible customers shall be able to submit 1–5 star ratings and written reviews for purchased products.

FR-20

Notifications

The system shall send relevant email, SMS or push notifications for registration, order, payment, shipping, delivery, cancellation, return and refund events.

6. Order Lifecycle

Order Placed → Confirmed → Packed → Shipped → Out for Delivery → Delivered

7. Admin Requirements

7.1 Product Management

Add products

Edit products

Delete/deactivate products

Update prices

Manage inventory

7.2 User Management

View users

Activate/deactivate users

View user details

7.3 Order Management

View orders

Update order status

View cancelled orders

View returned orders

View refund status

7.4 Reports

Sales report

Product report

Customer report

Order report

Revenue report

Return/refund report

8. Non-Functional Requirements

Area

Requirement

Performance

Pages and search results should respond within acceptable limits under normal load.

Security

Use secure password storage, role-based access control, protected APIs and secure handling of sensitive data.

Availability

Application should provide high availability and minimize downtime.

Scalability

System should support growth in users, products, orders and transactions.

Usability

Application should provide simple navigation, responsive UI, clear errors and consistent design.

9. Assumptions

Users have internet connectivity.

Payment gateway services are available.

Delivery partners are integrated with the system.

Sellers provide accurate product information.

Users provide valid delivery details.

Product inventory is updated regularly.

10. Dependencies

Payment Gateway

SMS Gateway

Email Service

Maps/Location Service

Delivery/Logistics Service

Database

Authentication Service

11. Risks and Mitigation

Risk

Impact

Mitigation

Payment failure

High

Retry and payment-status handling

Server downtime

High

High-availability infrastructure

Incorrect inventory

High

Real-time inventory updates

Security breach

Critical

Security controls, access control and monitoring

Delivery delay

Medium

Logistics tracking and status visibility

High traffic

High

Scalable infrastructure and performance testing

12. Acceptance Criteria

Users can successfully register and log in.

Users can search, filter and sort products.

Users can add, update and remove products from the cart.

Users can successfully place orders.

Payment status is correctly captured.

Orders can be tracked.

Eligible orders can be cancelled or returned.

Refund status is correctly updated.

Admin can manage products and orders.

Critical and high-severity defects are resolved before release.

Security and performance requirements are satisfied.

13. Sample End-to-End Business Flow

User Registration → User Login → Browse / Search Product → View Product Details → Add to Cart → Select Address → Apply Coupon → Select Payment Method → Make Payment → Order Confirmation → Order Processing → Order Shipped → Out for Delivery → Order Delivered → Rating & Review

14. QA Traceability Example

BRD Requirement

Sample Test Scenario

FR-02 – User Login

Login with valid credentials

FR-02 – User Login

Login with invalid password

FR-03 – Product Search

Search using valid product keyword

FR-05 – Product Filtering

Filter products by price range

FR-08 – Add to Cart

Add an available product to cart

FR-12 – Checkout

Complete checkout with valid address

FR-13 – Payment

Complete payment using UPI

FR-15 – Order Tracking

Verify order status after shipment

FR-16 – Cancellation

Cancel an eligible order

FR-19 – Ratings

Submit rating after successful delivery

15. QA Process Mapping

BRD → Requirements → Test Scenarios → Test Cases → Automation → Test Execution → Defect Reporting → Retesting/Regression → RTM → Test Closure

16. Approval

Role

Name

Signature

Date

Business Owner







Project Manager







Business Analyst







QA Lead

Business Requirements Document (BRD)

AutomatiQA – AI-Powered Software Testing Platform

Project Name

AutomatiQA – AI-Powered Software Testing Platform

Business Objective

The objective of AutomatiQA is to simplify and automate software testing activities using artificial intelligence. The platform should help QA engineers, developers, and product teams reduce manual effort while improving test coverage and execution speed.

Business Requirements

Users must be able to create and manage testing projects within the platform. The system should allow users to upload requirement documents such as BRDs, user stories, and functional specifications.

AutomatiQA should analyze uploaded requirements and automatically generate relevant test scenarios and test cases using AI. Users should be able to review, edit, save, and execute generated test cases.

The platform should support multiple testing capabilities, including web UI testing, API testing, performance testing, and recorded browser workflows.

Users should also be able to select an AI provider and model, such as Gemini, OpenAI, or locally hosted Ollama models, based on available API credentials.

The system should provide dashboards displaying execution status, passed and failed tests, defects, and testing metrics.

Success Criteria

The solution should reduce manual test creation effort, improve requirement coverage, provide reusable test cases, and enable faster identification of application defects.

steps: Navigate to the OrangeHRM login page URL.

testCases.expectedResult: System displays an error message 'Invalid credentials' and user remains on the login page.

steps: Navigate to the OrangeHRM login page URL.

testCases.expectedResult: Monetary values render with exact currency symbols: '$' for USD, '€' for EUR, and '£' for GBP.
testCases.title: Verify standard currency symbol rendering for USD, EUR, and GBP
steps: Navigate to the application monetary display settings or financial dashboard.
Select or input a monetary value and set the active currency to USD.
Observe the rendered currency symbol in the UI.
Change the active currency to EUR and update the view.
Observe the rendered currency symbol in the UI.
Change the active currency to GBP and update the view.
Verify the rendered currency symbol in the UI for exact symbol matching.

testCases.expectedResult: Currency symbols ($ , € , £) are rendered clearly on the UI without layout breakage, overlap, or encoding glitches.
testDataSets: Set 1: Currency=USD, Amount=0.99, View Mode=Standard UI Card
Set 2: Currency=EUR, Amount=1000000.00, View Mode=Compact Data Grid
Set 3: Currency=GBP, Amount=50.25, View Mode=Summary Header Widget
steps: Navigate to the currency localization display page.
Select USD currency and enter a monetary value.
Inspect the UI element to ensure the '$' symbol is positioned correctly without truncation or character encoding errors.
Select EUR currency and enter a monetary value.
Inspect the UI element to ensure the '€' symbol displays correctly in the localized position.
Select GBP currency and enter a monetary value.
Inspect the UI element to ensure the '£' symbol renders with clean typography and spacing.
testCases.title: Verify UI symbol layout alignment and typography for supported currency symbols

steps: Navigate to the system currency preference configuration.
Attempt to set an invalid currency code or unsupported string into the monetary field.
Save changes and navigate to the monetary rendering UI.
Observe the UI rendering of the monetary amount.
testCases.title: Verify fallback behavior when invalid or unsupported currency code is provided
testCases.expectedResult: System handles unsupported currency codes gracefully by displaying default USD ($) symbol or presenting an appropriate error message without breaking UI layout.

testCases.title: Verify standard currency symbol and numeric value alignment in tabular views
steps: Navigate to the financial transactions list view page.
Ensure table rows contain monetary values with standard currency symbols.
Inspect the visual layout of the currency column across all displayed rows.
Verify that currency symbols and numeric values are consistently aligned (e.g. right-aligned for numbers with uniform symbol spacing).
testCases.expectedResult: Currency symbols and values align consistently without layout distortion or overlapping across all grid/table rows.
All currency codes, negative values, and decimal numbers maintain vertical alignment and proper spacing across all table rows.
testCases.title: Verify alignment for multi-character currency codes and negative values
steps: Navigate to the multi-currency report page.
Filter data to display mixed currency codes (e.g. USD, JPY, CAD) and negative balance formats.
Observe the alignment of decimal points and currency prefixes across consecutive rows.
Verify no line breaks occur between currency symbols/codes and numeric values.
testDataSets: Set 1: Currency = USD 1,000.00, EUR 2,500.50, Row Count = 15
Set 2: Currency = JPY 150000, INR 85,000.75, Row Count = 20
Set 3: Currency = CAD -1,250.00, AUD (500.25), Row Count = 30

testCases.title: Verify currency display alignment under window resizing and zoom levels
steps: Open the grid page displaying currency columns.
Adjust the browser viewport width and change browser zoom level.
Inspect currency columns across all table rows for overlapping, clipping, or distortion.
Verify that alignment and spacing rules remain intact across responsive breakpoints.
testCases.expectedResult: Currency symbols and amounts adjust responsively without line wrapping, overlapping, or clipping across all zoom levels.

apiScenarios.expectedResults: HTTP status code 200 OK. The response JSON contains 'userId' as integer 1, 'id' as integer 1, 'title' as non-empty string, and 'body' as non-empty string matching the post record.
apiScenarios.description:
[GET https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1]
Send a GET request to /posts/1 with no request payload to retrieve specific post details. Validate HTTP status code, headers, and ensure all expected response fields (userId, id, title, body) match the target data types and values.

apiScenarios.expectedResults: HTTP status code 404 Not Found. The response body is empty or returns an appropriate error message indicating that the resource does not exist.
apiScenarios.description:

apiScenarios.title: Verify API behavior when requesting a non-existent post ID
Verify successful retrieval of post by valid ID and validate response schema
apiScenarios.description:
[GET https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1]
Send a GET request to /posts/1 and verify that the API returns HTTP 200 status code with all expected attributes (userId, id, title, body) matching their respective data types and expected values.
apiScenarios.expectedResults: HTTP status code should be 200 OK. Response body must be a JSON object containing 'userId' (integer: 1), 'id' (integer: 1), 'title' (non-empty string), and 'body' (non-empty string). Content-Type header must be 'application/json'.

apiScenarios.title: Verify handling of non-existent post ID
apiScenarios.description:
[GET https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1]
Send a GET request with an out-of-range post ID (e.g., /posts/999999) to verify proper handling when a resource is not found.
apiScenarios.expectedResults: HTTP status code should be 404 Not Found. Response body should be empty or return an appropriate error message object.

apiScenarios.title: Verify handling of invalid/alphanumeric post ID
apiScenarios.description:
[GET https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1]
Send a GET request with an invalid non-integer post ID parameter (e.g., /posts/abc or /posts/-1) to test input validation and error handling.
apiScenarios.expectedResults: HTTP status code should be 400 Bad Request or 404 Not Found indicating the resource does not exist or the ID is invalid.
HTTP status code should be 200 OK. The returned payload should correctly represent post 1 without any error caused by the redundant body payload.
apiScenarios.description:
[GET https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1]
Send a GET request to /posts/1 with an empty or unexpected JSON body payload to ensure the server processes the GET request idempotently and correctly ignores the body.
apiScenarios.title: Verify request ignores unexpected body payload on GET request

apiScenarios.description:
[GET https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1]
Send a GET request to the '/posts/{id}' endpoint with a valid and existing post ID (e.g., 1).
apiScenarios.title: Verify successful retrieval of a post by a valid ID
apiScenarios.expectedResults: The API should respond with a 200 OK status code. The response payload should contain an object with 'userId', 'id', 'title', and 'body' fields, and the 'id' field should match the requested post ID. All fields should be present and not null.

apiScenarios.title: Validate response payload structure and data types for a successful post
apiScenarios.description:
[GET https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1]
After successfully retrieving a post using a valid ID, examine the structure and data types of the returned JSON object.
apiScenarios.expectedResults: The response payload must be a JSON object containing exactly four fields: 'userId' (integer), 'id' (integer), 'title' (string), and 'body' (string). All fields should have appropriate non-empty values matching their expected data types.

apiScenarios.title: Verify API behavior with a non-existent post ID
apiScenarios.expectedResults: The API should respond with a 404 Not Found status code. The response payload should be an empty JSON object or contain an appropriate error message indicating that the resource was not found.
apiScenarios.description:
[GET https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1]
Send a GET request to the '/posts/{id}' endpoint using an ID that does not correspond to any existing post (e.g., 999999).

apiScenarios.expectedResults: The API should respond with a 404 Not Found status code, indicating the resource could not be found or processed due to the invalid identifier. The response payload should be an empty JSON object or contain an appropriate error message.
apiScenarios.description:
[GET https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1]
Send a GET request to the '/posts/{id}' endpoint using a non-numeric or malformed ID (e.g., 'abc', '0', '-1').
apiScenarios.title: Verify API behavior with an invalid format for post ID
